text: “Thank goodness that it has finished, Miss Harcourt, ma’am,” Belinda the Fourth gasped, “and no matter what takes place from this point on, they are wedded safe and sound. Ma’am, the rice bags can be found in the pantry, the worn shoes sit behind the door, and the whipping cream has been placed on the sullar steps.”

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: When it reached 2:30, Mr. and Mrs. Stanhope departed, whereupon all the people traveled to Alder River so that they might bid them farewell on the train running in the afternoon. When Miss Rosalind . . . I ask her forgiveness, Mrs. Stanhope . . . walked out through the doorway belonging to the house of her youth, Hugh along with the girls cast the rice, while an old shoe was flung by Belinda the Fourth using such great accuracy that Mr. Wace was hit directly upon his head. It was Cedric, however, who held the role of providing the most charming farewell. He emerged suddenly from the porch while vigorously ringing a massive ancient brass dinner bell that had decorated the mantel in the dining room. Making a happy sound served as the sole intention of Cedric; yet when the loud noise faded, there echoed from the point, the bend, and the hill on the opposite side of the river the peeling of “fairy wedding bells,” which rang out in a clear, sweet, and increasingly faint manner, precisely as though the cherished echoes of Miss Rosalind were offering her a welcome and a goodbye. Thus, surrounded by this blessing composed of lovely noises, Miss Rosalind departed by carriage from her former existence filled with dreams and pretenses toward a richer existence of truths inside the active world outside.

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: A pair of hours afterward, Nell alongside Belinda the Fourth walked down the lane once more. Since Hugh had departed for West Welby to run a chore and Isolde was required to attend a home commitment, Nell and Belinda returned for the purpose of tidying up and securing the small stone dwelling. Late, golden sunlight flooded the garden, where bees hummed and butterflies fluttered; nevertheless, the small house held that elusive sense of gloom that invariably succeeds a celebration.

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: “My goodness, doesn't it seem deserted?” sobbed Belinda the Fourth, who had not stopped weeping throughout the entire trip back from the station. “When everything is finished, Miss Harcourt, ma'am, a wedding isn't really much happier than a funeral.”

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: An active night came next. It was necessary to take down the decorations, clean the dishes, and store the leftover treats in a basket to delight Belinda the Fourth’s younger brothers at their house. Nell refused to take a break before every last thing was in perfect condition; once Belinda had departed for home bearing her loot, Nell walked through the quiet rooms, experiencing the sensation of somebody stepping by themselves in an abandoned banquet hall, and pulled the blinds shut. Next, she secured the door with a key and took a seat beneath the silver poplar so she could await Hugh, experiencing great fatigue yet continuing to ponder “long, long thoughts” without growing weary.

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: “Nell, what is on your mind?” inquired Hugh, as he walked down the path. Outside by the road, he had left his buggy and horse.

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: “About Miss Rosalind and Mr. Stanhope,” Nell replied in a dreamy manner. “Is it not wonderful to consider the way all things have resolved . . . the manner in which they are reunited at last following every year of distance and misapprehension?”

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: “Indeed, it is lovely,” stated Hugh, gazing intently down at the raised face of Nell, “yet would it not have been even finer, Nell, had no rift or misapprehension ever occurred . . . had they traveled side by side through their entire existence, possessing no recollections from the past except the ones they shared together?”

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: Nell’s heart beat strangely for an instant, her eyes wavering beneath Hugh’s look for the very first time as a pink blush colored her pale face. A curtain suspended before her internal awareness seemed to rise, exposing hidden emotions and truths to her sight. Maybe romance failed to arrive in a person's existence with fanfare and pageantry, resembling a splendid knight riding forth; maybe it slipped to a person's flank through peaceful paths like an ancient companion; maybe it manifested as ordinary writing, right up until an abrupt beam of light cast across the sheets revealed the cadence and the melody, maybe . . . maybe . . . love blossomed effortlessly from a lovely companionship, just as a yellow-centered rose emerges from its calyx.

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: Afterwards the curtain fell once more; yet the Nell who trod the gloomy avenue was not entirely the identical Nell who had ridden merrily along it the previous night. An invisible hand had flipped the leaf of girlhood, leaving the leaf of womanhood lying open in front of her, complete with its fascination and secrecy, its suffering and joy.

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: Hugh prudently refrained from further speech; nevertheless, within his quietude, he foresaw the events of the subsequent four years through the memory of Nell’s rosy cheeks. Four years filled with dedicated, joyful labor . . . followed ultimately by the reward of practical wisdom acquired and a tender heart secured.

chapter_title: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
text: In the garden behind them, the small house of stone brooded amidst the shadows. Though lonely, it was not abandoned. Dreams, laughter, and the zest for life were not yet finished with it; upcoming summers awaited the small house of stone; for now, it was able to wait. And across the river, held in purple captivity, the echoes awaited their moment.
